failedGraders: judge:A push-device registry slice was just added to the notifications context (packages/api/typescript). Verify ALL of: (a) DI-REG — src/notifications/registry.ts binds PushDeviceRepository in ALL THREE environment arrays with the sibling { token, instance } shape: mock resolves MockPushDeviceRepository, integration AND real resolve DrizzlePushDeviceRepository; nothing else registers the repository (no shared/registry.ts edits — notifications is already aggregated; no registerInstance calls in src or tests); the abstract PushDeviceRepository class is the DI token everywhere — the use case constructor and the tests depend on it, never on the Mock/Drizzle concretes. (b) TEST-MODE placement — PushDevice.test.ts is a pure unit spec (direct instantiation, no TestBed, no DI container); DrizzlePushDeviceRepository.test.ts and RegisterPushDevice.test.ts boot TestBed.create('integration', ...) ONCE per suite on a child container in beforeAll, with beforeEach(testBed.reset()) and afterAll(testBed.destroy()), and resolve the repository/use case via testBed.resolve. Prerequisite state is built via given helpers only: the FK-satisfying user rows come from givenUser/givenUserWithAccount (directly or inside givenPushDevice), pre-existing devices come from givenPushDevice, and givenPushDevice itself persists through PushDeviceRepository — the use-case test NEVER builds fixture state by calling RegisterPushDevice (or any other use case) before the scenario's single action under test. (c) Use-case test scope — RegisterPushDevice.test.ts covers orchestration only: first registration persists (read back through the resolved PushDeviceRepository), same-user re-register is idempotent (refreshes liveness, no duplicate row/entity), different-user conflict rejects with name 'PUSH_TOKEN_ALREADY_REGISTERED' via expect(...).rejects.toMatchObject; there is NO re-testing of entity-level validation (empty token, bad platform, VALIDATION_ERROR cases) at use-case level — those invariants live in PushDevice.test.ts. (d) Repository canon — the abstract class extends Repository<PushDevice> and only adds finder signatures (optional tx param, Promise<... | undefined>, no save/delete redeclarations); DrizzlePushDeviceRepository is @injectable with DrizzleClient constructor injection, wraps queries in tryCatchAsync, uses tx ?? this.db, maps rows via toDomain passing raw primitives into new PushDevice (never PushDevice.create), maps out via toPersistence, and save calls entity.incrementVersion() then insert().values().onConflictDoUpdate; MockPushDeviceRepository is a real in-memory implementation whose semantics match (including the token-uniqueness lookup). (e) Use case + error vocabulary — RegisterPushDevice extends Handler with exported Input/Output schemas (input keeps wire primitives: z.uuid() for userId, z.enum(FcmPlatform) for platform — no z.instance in the input), a snake_case readonly name, all DB work inside withTransaction with tx passed to EVERY repository call including the findByPushToken pre-check; the idempotent branch mutates through an entity behavior method (no property assignment in the use case); the conflict throws BaseError typed with the context error union, and 'PUSH_TOKEN_ALREADY_REGISTERED' is added to the notifications errors/index.ts union AND registered in registerErrorCodes mapped to CONFLICT. Scope notes — legitimate exceptions, do NOT fail these: the notifications.push_devices table has NO version/created_at/updated_at columns (legacy shape, intentionally unmigrated), so the Drizzle save omitting version/updatedAt from the onConflictDoUpdate set and toDomain not passing audit fields is the EXPECTED shape — incrementVersion() being called without a persisted version column is correct here, not a bug. The Drizzle repository test MAY construct PushDevice.create(...) inline for the aggregate under test and MAY resolve DrizzleClient — both are sanctioned for Drizzle*Repository.test.ts files. The use-case test calling useCase.execute() as the action under test (once per scenario) is the point of the test, not a fixture violation. Reusing the FcmPlatform wire enum for the platform field is the prescribed shape — do not fail naming consistency over the 'Fcm' prefix. A domain event in RegisterPushDevice is OPTIONAL: absence is fine, and if present it must be persisted via this.domainEventRepository.save(event, tx) (only direct mediator publishing fails). Any ownerId string passed to TestBed.create is fine. Judge the idiom, not variable names — local aliases (repo vs repository vs deviceRepo) are fine. Inspect the new files under src/notifications/{entities,repositories/PushDeviceRepository,usecases} plus src/notifications/registry.ts, src/notifications/errors/index.ts, the touched barrels, and tests/support/given/{notifications.ts,index.ts}. Pre-existing notifications artifacts (Notification*, SendNotification, MarkNotificationRead, PushDeliveryService) and the identity FCM slice are out of scope.

judge:A Finance cost-source digest projection was just added under packages/api/typescript/src/finance/projections/. Verify ALL of: (a) PROJECTION SHAPE — CostDigest.ts holds a flat Zod schema with the Props type inferred from it, an exported CostDigestProjectionEvent union built from the REAL event classes imported from the finance events module (a union over wrapper/subclass types defined locally to re-type the events is a violation), and a free-record class (no base class, no @injectable, no validation, no throws, no domain events) whose constructor takes the full props; static create is ONE overloaded method (one signature per creating event — OperationalCostCreated and WarrantyReserveCreated — plus a single implementation switching on the event name) and applyEvent is ONE overloaded method covering every mutating event it handles, mutating this.props only. (b) PROJECTOR DISPATCH — CostDigestProjector extends Projector<CostDigestProjectionEvent> with the generic imported from the projection file (no duplicated local union), takes the CostDigestProjectionRepository as its ONLY constructor dependency, declares readonly events listing all six wire names (finance.operational_cost.created/updated/deleted + finance.warranty_reserve.created/updated/deleted), and handle() is a plain switch on the event name: creation cases call repo.insertIfNew with CostDigestProjection.create(event), every mutating case follows find -> applyEvent -> save with a SILENT no-op return when the row is missing (never a throw), and the default branch enforces exhaustiveness by assigning the narrowed event to never. (c) ATOMIC DISCIPLINE — the repository exposes the canonical trio (a natural-key finder, save, insertIfNew with ON-CONFLICT-DO-NOTHING semantics) as one abstract class with Mock + Drizzle implementations; NONE of the six digest events is hot-row/bulk/monotonic/conditional/ cache-mirror, so the expected shape is ZERO atomic mutation ops — if any extra write method exists beyond the trio it must carry a written comment naming one of the five triggers AND the trigger must plausibly hold for this workload; a repo-level UPDATE verb substituting for applyEvent on a single-row mutation is a fail. (d) ASYNC-INLINE — the projector reaches the outbox via the projectors slot of BoundedContext.create in src/finance/index.ts and the projections/projectors/index.ts barrel; NO finance use case, controller or handler imports or invokes the projector or the projection repository (this brief has no read-after-write need, so any inline projector.handle(event, tx) call inside a use case is a fail); registry.ts binds CostDigestProjectionRepository for all three environments (Mock impl for mock, Drizzle impl for integration and real). (e) DISCRIMINANT FIX — the event-union narrowing compiles because the events got literal instance name types at the source (e.g. a type-only declare of the instance name on the six finance event classes, or an equivalent fix in the shared base) — NOT via as-casts, @ts-expect-error/@ts-ignore, instanceof/if-else chains replacing the switch, or wrapper subclasses local to the projection files. (f) SUPERSESSION + DELETES — the WarrantyReserveCreated case both inserts the new row AND, when previousWarrantyReserveId is non-null, transitions the predecessor row so it no longer reads as the active reserve; the two Deleted cases mark the row inactive/deleted while keeping it (no SQL DELETE of digest rows); the Drizzle table in packages/contracts/db/schema/finance.ts mirrors the projection schema field-for-field and a generated migration creates the finance.cost_digest table. (g) TESTS — CostDigest.test.ts unit-tests the projection by direct instantiation (no TestBed, no I/O) covering each create overload and each applyEvent transition; CostDigestProjector.test.ts runs in TestBed integration mode, drives every subscribed event through projector.handle, and proves replay-safety (handling the same event twice yields one row / the same final state). Scope notes — judge the idiom, not the spelling: the events array referencing the event classes' static name constants instead of literal strings is canon (the overridden static names ARE the dotted wire strings); implementing the supersession transition as an atomic conditional repo op is acceptable ONLY with a written trigger justification comment — canonical find -> applyEvent -> save needs no justification and is the default expectation; a read-only finder or list helper on the repository used by tests or by the projector's find half is NOT an atomic mutation op — do not flag it; `as` casts on raw DB rows inside the Drizzle repository's toDomain/toPersistence mapping are the scaffold's established shape — the cast ban in (e) concerns the event discriminant and dispatch, not row mapping; the projector being invoked as handle(event) without a transaction on the outbox path is expected — do not require tx threading everywhere. Inspect the new files under src/finance/projections/, the touched src/finance/events/*.ts, src/finance/index.ts, src/finance/registry.ts, packages/contracts/db/schema/finance.ts and the newest migration under packages/contracts/db/migrations/.

judge:A Sales Reports page was just added under packages/app/react/src/routes/(app)/reports/. Verify ALL of: (a) UI-COMPOSITION — the route index.tsx is a thin shell: the URL contract (validateSearch with the recorte field typed against the SDK ChartType values and defaulted, dates defaulted to a last-30-days window) plus layout composition only — no SDK hook calls, no business JSX in the route; a Section component under -components/ owns the single useGetChart query; static UI (page header, recorte selector) stays visible while data loads, with an inline NON-exported skeleton in the data-dependent area only, and the data area follows skeleton -> empty -> content (an empty state where a member can be genuinely empty, e.g. income buckets / region rows). (b) DATA-OWNERSHIP — the section reads recorte/dates via the route's search hook and tenancyScope via a useTenancyStore selector; exactly ONE component calls useGetChart; the route never fetches and passes data down; recorte changes write through router navigation (a search updater or Link), never component state; variant components receive the ALREADY-FETCHED response (or their member of it) by prop and never re-fetch; no useState and no new Zustand store anywhere under the new directory. (c) DISC-UNION + CENTRALIZE-MAPS — each of the five kinds renders through its own variant sub-component, selected via ONE module-level dispatch map keyed by the SDK ChartType (exhaustive — a new kind must break tsc), not via a switch or an if/else-if chain across kinds inline in a single component; no all-optional flattened row type that merges the five members; no hand-rolled parallel union re-declaring the SDK kinds; no casts (as any / as never / as unknown) to force the map-lookup correlation. (d) LOCALE-MONEY + ENUM-REPR — every monetary value renders through the useMoney() formatter (the SignedMoney object handed over as-is; no amountCents/100 hand-math, no toFixed, no direct formatMoney import from @/lib/format inside components); income bucket date labels format with the active locale obtained from useLocale() — never a hardcoded 'pt-BR'/'en-US' or a date-fns locale object; the recorte option labels come from the i18n enums.ChartType.* catalog with entries present in BOTH src/locales/pt.json and en.json; weekday/day-part segment labels are translated via i18n keys, not hardcoded strings. Scope notes — judge the idiom, not the variable name: a variant sub-component receiving the fetched response or its narrowed member as a prop is the EXPECTED CMP-P18/CMP-P05 shape — do not fail it as prop-drilling. Because TypeScript cannot correlate a map lookup with a union-typed prop, BOTH cast-free typings pass: a map of uniform-signature views that each take the full response and guard their own kind with an early return (if (data.kind !== 'weekday') return null), OR Extract-typed variant props with the correlation resolved type-safely — do not fail the single-kind guard as an "if chain"; what fails is one component branching across MULTIPLE kinds inline, or flattening. tenancyScope living in the app-global Zustand store (useTenancyStore) instead of the URL is the house canon — do not fail it. A const-asserted ordering array for fixed segment keys (MONDAY..SUNDAY, MORNING..NIGHT, hour sorting) resolves ORDER, not labels — fine. Hardcoding frequency: 'DAILY' in the query params is per the brief — fine. The dispatch map spelling may be Record<ChartType, ...>, satisfies Record<...>, or a mapped type keyed by ChartType — all fine. The pre-existing dashboard chart (src/routes/(app)/dashboard/-components/RevenueChartSection/) carries known deviations and is OUT of scope — judge only the new files under src/routes/(app)/reports/ plus src/locales/pt.json and en.json.

judge:A Reports deep-dive page was just added under packages/app/react/src/routes/(app)/reports/. Verify ALL of: (a) SCHEMA-DERIVE / state-placement case 2 — the route index.tsx is a thin shell (URL contract + layout composition only, no SDK hook calls, no business JSX); the search schema is COMPOSED from the wire contract: it starts from an SDK query-params schema (getChartQueryParamsSchema or listQuickProductRankingQueryParamsSchema), .omit()s tenancyScope plus any required field being re-defaulted, and .and()s the route-local fields; the WHOLE schema parses from an empty search object — every re-added field carries .default() (period defaults to the last 30 days, granularity to a daily-equivalent), including the frequency field typed by the SDK AnalyticsFrequency enum — never a hand-rolled z.object duplicating fields the SDK schema already declares while ignoring it; period + granularity are READ in section components via useSearch and WRITTEN via navigate with a functional search update, so the filtered view deep-links and survives refresh; tenancyScope never appears in the URL schema and IS read from the app-global useTenancyStore via a selector at the analytics query call sites — the omit is a relocation, not a deletion. (b) state-placement case 3 — the comparison basket lives in ONE route-scoped Zustand store under -stores/ holding only the selected product ids plus actions (including a clear/reset); components access it with selectors; it is read by at least the ranking table rows, the toolbar (count + clear) and the comparison panel; it is NOT in the URL, NOT a useState lifted into the page, and NOT prop-drilled callbacks from a stateful parent; no server data is mirrored into the store (no row objects, no query responses) — the comparison panel derives its rows from its own SDK query data filtered by the stored ids. (c) FORM-SUBSCRIBE / state-placement case 4 — the inline target editor owns a TanStack useForm validated by createGoalMutationRequestSchema (the SDK schema, no parallel hand-rolled schema); the implied daily run-rate preview and the unsaved-changes banner derive from form state via form.Subscribe with narrow selectors (value slices / isDirty) — they are NEVER mirrored into useState or a store by onChange handlers, and there are no raw form.state.values reads in render bodies; the submit button is gated per FRM-P03 (form.Subscribe + safeParse) and the mutation sends validated data. (d) DATA-OWNERSHIP + MUTATION-IDIOM — each section owns its own query (chart owns useGetChart with chartType income, ranking owns useListQuickProductRanking, the target card owns useGetGoal); no query data is prop-drilled between sections (leaf rows receiving their item from the list-owning parent is fine); pending state renders inline skeletons; the CreateGoal mutation invalidates the goal read via getGoalQueryKey on success/settled, in-flight feedback comes from the hook's isPending, and there is no try/catch and no onError handler. (e) ENUM-REPR + LOCALE — the granularity options derive from the SDK enum (Select enum={AnalyticsFrequencyEnum} / Object.values / analyticsFrequencySchema.options — never a hand-typed parallel value array); labels come from the typed i18n catalog (enums.AnalyticsFrequency.* with keys in BOTH src/locales/pt.json and en.json; the target type via enums.GoalType.*); all user-facing copy is localized in both languages; money renders via useMoney(); no hardcoded 'pt-BR'/'en-US' anywhere under the new dir. (f) state-placement case 5 — zero useState under the route dir: this brief has no sanctioned transient (filters apply immediately, the editor is always visible, the basket is store-owned). Scope notes: the period/granularity filters are read by every section — that does NOT make them store state; URL placement is the expected shape, so do not fail (b) because the filters are not in the store. The run-rate preview and dirty banner render inside the target card only — form.Subscribe is the expected mechanism; do not fail (c) for the preview not being shared through a store, and do not demand it render outside the form component. tenancyScope still reaches the wire as a query param on every analytics call — store-owned means URL-omitted, not wire-omitted; do not fail (a) for tenancyScope appearing in hook params. productIds inherited from the SDK schema part may survive in the composed schema as optional WITHOUT .default(), or be omitted entirely — both are acceptable; the every-field-defaulted bar applies to the re-added route-local fields. Local naming varies (store, action, selector and component names) — judge the idiom, not the name. Pre-existing files (the dashboard route including its useState fallbacks, components/drawers/GoalDrawer, the Header/Navbar) are OUT of scope; judge only the files under src/routes/(app)/reports/ plus src/locales/pt.json and en.json.
